.github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on pull_request to main, installs with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and caches the pnpm store via setup-node's cache: pnpm, then runs typecheck, format:check, test and build. The workflow has never executed (no PR yet), so I verified what I could: all three action major tags resolve (actions/checkout@v7, actions/setup-node@v7, pnpm/action-setup@v6 — HTTP 200 each) and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds locally, which is the step most likely to break CI.
Read the workflow line by line: no continue-on-error, no `||`, no `set +e`, no composite step that could swallow an exit code. Each gate is its own step, so any non-zero exit fails the job.

setup-node uses node-version-file: .nvmrc, and pnpm/action-setup is deliberately given no `version:` input so it reads the root packageManager field. Both are commented in the workflow with the reason.

harness.config.yml declares gates as exactly [typecheck, 'format:check', test, build] and carries no `merge:` block, so merge.allow_no_checks stays at its default false. Read the committed file directly.

findings.summary: The destructive confirm's `default: false` — the keystroke that separates cancel from delete — has no automated assertion; flipping it to true leaves the suite 7/7 green.

Result assertions use toEqual rather than toStrictEqual, so an unexpected undefined-valued property would pass; same pattern at clean-database.spec.ts:31/44, check-connection.spec.ts:17, client.spec.ts:39/51/73.

The menu dispatch is an if-chain with no terminal else, so an unrecognised choice would spin the for(;;) loop silently instead of failing loudly. Unreachable today (the value set is a closed typed union), so hardening rather than a bug.

R48 PARTIAL: implemented correctly and demonstrated in the real run, but untested — the mutation to `default: true` survived. The gap sits inside design.md's human-approved "prompt layer not tested, by decision", so it is a specified gap, not an implementer omission.

R44 covers Ctrl+C only and is satisfied; stdin EOF (Ctrl+D) is unspecified and exits 13 with an "unsettled top-level await" warning. Not a compliance failure, but it is absent from progress.md, which R58/R59 make the durable real-run record.

Medium / hardening: `- '27017:27017'` publishes the credential-less MongoDB on all interfaces (0.0.0.0), so on any shared or untrusted network every host on the LAN gets unauthenticated full read/write on every database. The header comment warns against copying the file to a reachable environment, but the default binding already makes the dev machine reachable. `'127.0.0.1:27017:27017'` closes it while still satisfying R22's port publication and R28's mongodb://localhost:27017/memora.

Low / informational: the shadcn components take `cn` from a third-party npm package rather than a local src/lib/utils.ts. Provenance checked and clean — npm metadata resolves to github.com/shadcn-ui/cn and the lockfile integrity hash matches the registry's exactly — but it is a new supply-chain edge on a very short package name, worth pinning exactly (it currently carries a caret).

Low / informational, named per §11: `onlyBuiltDependencies: [esbuild, lightningcss]` re-enables dependency install scripts for those two packages, which is executable code running at install time. Narrow, deliberate and documented in the file; no other package regains that privilege.
Pass 5: the menu dispatch has no terminal else, so an unrecognised choice would loop silently rather than fail loudly. Unreachable with today's closed typed union — hardening, not a live bug.

The only logic-bearing file in the change with no dedicated spec — and seven requirements ride on it (R38, R39, R41 wiring, R42 wiring, R44, R47, R48). design.md excludes it by decision, so the gap is specified; its whole protection is the one-off manual run recorded in progress.md, which does not regress. Cheapest closure without a TTY: extract the confirm's options (or a buildCleanConfirm(database) factory) and assert default === false and that the message names the database.

The db:* scripts and the compose manifest have no automated coverage at all (hermeticity forbids it, R56), so R24-R27 rest entirely on the recorded real run. Accepted as a deliberate consequence of the hermetic-suite requirement, noted so it is visible rather than implicit.
